correctness.rationale: On real \(\ell_4^3(\mathbb R)\), the numerical-abscissa quotient is \(F/Q\). In antisymmetric and symmetric coordinates, \(F=2ab(a^2+3w^2-b^2)\) and \(Q=2a^4+b^4+12a^2w^2+2w^4\). Two exact polynomial sum-of-squares identities force the positive-sign branch below \(1/2\). The negative-sign branch strictly decreases in the symmetric-mode square and attains its maximum on the invariant antisymmetric plane. The strictly monotone critical polynomial \(2\rho^3-6\rho^2-3\rho+1\) has a unique root in \((0,1)\), yielding the exact extremal scalar and all normers. Quartic differentiation plus an extremizing initial tangent establishes the all-time optimal prefactor-one semigroup growth bound. Skew symmetry supplies Euclidean orthogonality and the spectrum. The bundled standard-library checker passed 15,626 finite assertions; these are supplementary to the universal analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2026 full text proves general Banach-space numerical-range facts and a different two-dimensional semigroup example. The fully inspected classical real \(L_p\) paper provides a two-coordinate skew-rotation benchmark, but does not prove reduction of this three-coordinate ambient problem. The fully inspected prior three-point conditional-expectation commutator has a triangular three-edge skew matrix, not the present two-edge path: signed-permutation isometries of real \(\ell_4^3\) preserve the number of edges, and its exact scalar differs. The current strict positive-branch polynomial inequality and resulting single-ray normer rigidity are not entailed.
